finding: As of 2026-10-03 the latest ANNUAL release on the Data & Documentation page is the 2025 Annual Data Release (no 2026 annual release is listed). A 'Supplemental Data Release (March 2026)' analytic CSV (dated 2026-03-25) updates 50 measures with newer data years. The page also says the CHR&R Open Source Project on GitHub is meant to 'preserve, update and extend CHRR data assets beyond 2026'.
transform: percent measures = rawvalue x 100, 1 decimal; rates/days/years = rawvalue rounded to 1 decimal; ratios = population per provider (supplement: v0xx_rawalternatevalue; 2025 annual: v0xx_other_data_1) rounded to integer. Rounding done in JS with toFixed.

chr_poor_mh_days.name: Poor Mental Health Days
chr_poor_mh_days.def: Average number of mentally unhealthy days reported in past 30 days (age-adjusted).

chr_freq_mental_distress.name: Frequent Mental Distress
chr_freq_mental_distress.def: Percentage of adults reporting 14 or more days of poor mental health per month (age-adjusted).

chr_suicide_rate.name: Suicides
chr_suicide_rate.def: Number of deaths due to suicide per 100,000 population (age-adjusted).
chr_suicide_rate.source: National Center for Health Statistics - Mortality Files; Census Population Estimates Program

chr_drug_overdose_rate.name: Drug Overdose Deaths
chr_drug_overdose_rate.def: Number of drug poisoning deaths per 100,000 population.
chr_drug_overdose_rate.source: National Center for Health Statistics - Mortality Files; Census Population Estimates Program

chr_mh_provider_ratio.name: Mental Health Providers
chr_mh_provider_ratio.def: Ratio of population to mental health providers.
chr_mh_provider_ratio.source: CMS, National Provider Identifier Downloadable File

chr_pcp_ratio.name: Primary Care Physicians
chr_pcp_ratio.def: Ratio of population to primary care physicians.
chr_pcp_ratio.source: Area Health Resource File/American Medical Association

chr_uninsured_adults.name: Uninsured Adults
chr_uninsured_adults.def: Percentage of adults under age 65 without health insurance.

chr_excessive_drinking.name: Excessive Drinking
chr_excessive_drinking.def: Percentage of adults reporting binge or heavy drinking (age-adjusted).

chr_social_associations.name: Social Associations
chr_social_associations.def: Number of membership associations per 10,000 population.

chr_life_expectancy.name: Life Expectancy
chr_life_expectancy.def: Average number of years people are expected to live.
chr_life_expectancy.source: National Center for Health Statistics - Natality and Mortality Files; Census Population Estimates Program

chr_loneliness.name: Feelings of Loneliness
chr_loneliness.def: Percentage of adults reporting that they always, usually or sometimes feel lonely.

chr_lack_social_support.name: Lack of Social and Emotional Support
chr_lack_social_support.def: Percentage of adults reporting that they sometimes, rarely, or never get the social and emotional support they need.

chr_children_poverty.name: Children in Poverty
chr_children_poverty.def: Percentage of people under age 18 in poverty.
chr_children_poverty.source: Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates; American Community Survey, five-year estimates

chr_severe_housing.name: Severe Housing Problems
chr_severe_housing.def: Percentage of households with at least 1 of 4 housing problems: overcrowding, high housing costs, lack of kitchen facilities, or lack of plumbing facilities.

chr_pct_rural.name: % Rural
chr_pct_rural.def: Percentage of population living in a census-defined rural area.
chr_pct_rural.source: Decennial Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics File

observations: Supplement: Coosa (01037) and Lamar (01075) have v004_numerator = 0 (zero primary care physicians) and blank rawvalue/rawalternatevalue; the same two are blank in the 2025 annual file. Empty cell = no ratio can be formed (0 physicians), not suppression.
Supplement: Connecticut state row has blank provider ratios (v062, v004); codebook says Connecticut was not fully updated in the supplemental releases.

Supplement: Kentucky and Pennsylvania state rows are blank for BRFSS-based 2023 measures (poor mental health days, frequent mental distress, excessive drinking, loneliness, social support). Loneliness / social-support are blank for CO, FL, KY, OR, PA, SD, TN, TX, VT, WA, WY (11 states) in the supplement and for AR, CO, HI, IL, LA, NY, ND, OR, PA, SD, VA in the 2025 annual file.
Supplement: District of Columbia state-level row has an empty name field (statecode 11, state DC).

State-level BRFSS values moved a lot between 2025 annual (2022 data) and the supplement (2023 data): e.g. California poor mental health days 4.7 -> 5.7 and frequent mental distress 14.6 -> 18.4; US 5.1 -> 5.7 days and 16.3 -> 18.6 percent. County values for Alabama moved the other way (67-county mean poor MH days 6.24 -> 5.84). Looks like a methodology change rather than a real one-year shift; do not compare across the two releases.
Alabama county suicide rate is suppressed (blank) for 12 counties and drug overdose rate for 19 counties in the supplement.
